q: What carbon data do Ruhr steelmakers ask ore and ferroalloy suppliers for?
title: Ruhr steelmakers: supplier carbon data
short: Mostly product footprints per tonne for their own Scope 3 and low carbon steel claims, and CBAM embedded emissions for covered goods such as pellets and ferroalloys. Iron ore fines are not a CBAM good, but buyers still want mining, processing and shipping emissions.
audience: Iron ore, pellet and ferroalloy suppliers in India, South Africa and elsewhere selling to German steelmakers

ul: Agglomerated ore (pellets, sinter) and ferroalloys: CBAM embedded emissions per tonne.
Their own Scope 1 and 2 behind that figure.
Iron ore fines and lump: mining diesel, beneficiation electricity, rail and sea freight.
Coking coal: mining methane and transport.

p: Ruhr mills switching to DRI and arc furnaces sell low carbon steel on a cradle to gate figure, so every input's footprint now shows up in their price.

senseible: Senseible reads your electricity bills and fuel invoices into Scope 1 and 2 records with the factor and source on each line, the site data a buyer questionnaire starts from. It does not produce verified product footprints or fill a buyer's portal for you.
